sources.entry: SaneBar - Privacy-first menu bar manager with Touch ID lock, Always-Hidden Zone, and automation triggers.

summary.one_liner: SaneBar is a free, open-source (MIT) macOS menu bar manager that hides and reveals menu bar icons, with Touch ID lock, smart triggers, and profiles.
summary.what_it_does: SaneBar lets you hide menu bar apps you do not need right now and keep important ones visible. You can ⌘+drag icons to choose which stay visible, and click the SaneBar icon to show or hide the rest. Hidden icons can be browsed in either a floating Icon Panel or a Second Menu Bar row, with search, drag reordering, and double-click to open. A Find Icon search can virtually click apps even when they sit behind the notch. The README also lists Always Hidden zones, Touch ID/password lock for hidden icons, smart triggers (Focus Mode, Wi-Fi, app launch, low battery, external monitor, scripts), profiles, per-icon hotkeys, icon groups, and AppleScript automation. Settings can be exported and imported, and Bartender or Ice settings can be imported.
use_cases: hide menu bar icons on a crowded Mac
lock hidden menu bar apps behind Touch ID
find a menu bar app hidden behind the notch
automatically show icons based on Wi-Fi or Focus mode
replace Bartender or Ice with a free alternative
script menu bar visibility with AppleScript
how_to_run: git clone the repository and cd SaneBar
notable: Fully free and MIT licensed, with no license key, trial, or subscription
Touch ID / Password lock for hidden menu bar icons
Two viewing modes: Icon Panel and Second Menu Bar
Find Icon search that clicks icons even when hidden behind the notch
Smart triggers and profiles, plus Bartender and Ice settings import
caveats: Requires macOS 14.0 through macOS 26 on Apple Silicon only; on macOS 27 it shows a notice instead of hiding icons
Community-maintained now; the README says the sanebar.com site and update feed are best-effort and may lapse
Building from source needs Xcode 16+ and macOS Sequoia or later
